title: Publish work schedules two weeks ahead
action: Employers post hourly shifts 14 days in advance and leave workers free to swap shifts voluntarily.
measure: Median days of notice and share of shifts changed at the employer's request.
question: If demand changes after the schedule goes up, how would a manager find volunteers and track who asked for the change?
aliases: when do I work next week
example: Imagine arranging a ride to work and finding out the night before that your shift has moved.

title: Tie childcare bills to family income
action: A state funds licensed places with a sliding family payment and pays providers the balance of an agreed rate.
measure: Family cost as a share of income and how many families are waiting.
question: If a parent's hours vary, how often should the family payment change, and how would the provider get paid on time?

title: Allow smaller homes near jobs and transit
action: Cities allow duplexes and small apartment buildings on suitable serviced lots through a predictable approval process.
measure: Homes completed and the rents or sale prices people actually pay.
question: Which lots already have the utilities for more homes, and what would builders need to know before buying one?

title: Let hourly workers earn paid sick time
action: Employers or states offer paid sick time that builds with hours worked, including part-time shifts.
measure: Share of hourly staff able to take a sick shift with pay.
question: How could someone working short shifts check their balance and use sick time without losing that shift's pay?

title: Keep primary care open after work
action: Community clinics test evening and Saturday appointments with the visit price or sliding fee available at booking.
measure: Time to the next affordable appointment outside working hours.
question: Which evening or Saturday hours would patients use, and how could the clinic cover them while keeping visits affordable?
example: Imagine finding a clinic you can afford, then learning its last appointment starts before your shift ends.

title: Get unpaid wages back faster
action: State labor agencies assign a case owner to wage claims and fast-track documented underpayments with an opportunity for both sides to respond.
measure: Days to actual repayment and wages returned.
question: What could a worker submit if their hours and pay stub disagree, and how would the employer correct an error?
example: Imagine your pay stub shows fewer hours than you worked, and rent is due before your claim can be heard.

title: Run buses for the first and last shifts
action: A transit agency and major workplaces align a pilot route with early starts and late finishes in both directions.
measure: Shift changes served and completed rides per service dollar.
question: Which later trip would get riders home, and who would cover the driver's time if fares fall short?
example: Imagine your shift ends ten minutes after the last bus leaves.

title: Cover a short rent gap before eviction
action: A county makes small emergency rent payments quickly enough to help eligible households stay in their homes.
measure: Days to payment and households still housed 90 days later.
question: What proof could a household supply quickly enough for the county to pay before an eviction proceeds?

title: Link the minimum wage to inflation
action: A state adopts a published annual adjustment so workers and employers can plan for changes in the cost of living.
measure: Inflation-adjusted earnings and paid hours near the wage floor.
question: Which price index and notice date would make the adjustment understandable when people plan next year's pay and hours?

title: Show the full monthly rent up front
action: Housing agencies and landlords pilot listings that include every mandatory monthly fee and separately disclose required move-in charges.
measure: Difference between the advertised monthly total and the signed lease.
question: How would a renter tell which charges recur every month and which are due only when signing?

title: Pay apprentices from their first day
action: Employers and training providers offer paid apprenticeships with a published wage ladder and a recognized credential.
measure: Completion rate and earnings six months after completion.
question: Who would cover paid training time, and when would an apprentice qualify for the next wage step?
aliases: get paid to learn a trade

title: Replace wages during family or medical leave
action: A state insurance program replaces a larger share of lower paychecks during qualifying illness, new parenthood or family caregiving.
measure: Take-up among lower-paid workers and income replaced.
question: What payment and application timetable would let someone on a small paycheck afford their first week of leave?
aliases: paid time to care for a parent

title: Serve school breakfast and lunch to every student
action: A state and school district cover the cost so any student can eat without a family application or a charge at the register.
measure: Meals eaten, student participation and cost per meal.
question: Can kitchens serve everyone within the breakfast and lunch periods, and what staff or equipment would that take?

title: Check for hospital discounts before collections
action: Hospitals help patients check eligibility for financial assistance and resolve the application before referring a bill for collection.
measure: Eligible bills reduced before collection and days to a decision.
question: How would the billing team pause a referral if a patient is still gathering documents for a discount?

title: Get the first unemployment check out on time
action: A state agency flags delayed claims for a trained examiner who can resolve missing information by phone.
measure: Days from a valid claim to first payment and rate of incorrect decisions.
question: How would an examiner reach someone who misses a call and resolve the claim without sending them to the back of the queue?

title: Fund childcare on nights and weekends
action: Counties and shift employers purchase reserved places from licensed providers and fund the staffing those hours require.
measure: Requested off-hours places filled and cost per occupied place.
question: Which nights and weekends would families book, and who would pay for staff when a reserved place goes unused?
example: Imagine being offered a Sunday shift when the daycare you use is closed.

title: Put a real pay range in every job listing
action: Employers publish a good-faith base-pay range before asking people to apply and list tips, bonuses or commission separately.
measure: Share of offers within the posted range.
question: How would a hiring team set a useful range and explain any offer outside it?

title: Fix the car that gets someone to work
action: Local workforce agencies fund capped, independently quoted essential repairs when a broken car threatens a job and transit is unavailable.
measure: Days of work missed and recipients still employed after 90 days.
question: Who could approve an essential repair quickly enough to save a shift, and how would they check the quote?
aliases: car broke down can't get to work

title: Let renters reuse a screening report
action: Participating landlords accept one renter-authorized, correctable report for 30 days so a housing search incurs fewer application fees.
measure: Screening fees paid per successful move.
question: How would renters correct an error and let a second landlord use the report before it expires?

title: Cut utility bills in drafty homes
action: Utilities and local housing programs fund insulation and air sealing in eligible homes, including rentals where tenants pay the energy bills.
measure: Weather-adjusted bill changes and household out-of-pocket cost.
question: In a rental, who would approve the work, and how would the program check the savings on the tenant's bill?

title: Keep after-school care open through the workday
action: School districts and local providers extend affordable pickup hours to match when families can get back from work.
measure: Unmet requests and hours of coverage added per family.
question: Which pickup times would cover the trip home from work, and how would the provider staff the last hour?
aliases: school lets out before work ends

title: Show both prices for the same prescription
action: Participating pharmacies offer a comparison of the cash price and the patient's insurance copay for the same drug and quantity before checkout.
measure: Out-of-pocket difference when a lower price is available.
question: How would the pharmacist show both prices and explain what a cash purchase would mean for the patient's deductible?

title: Ease the loss of benefits after a raise
action: A state tests a temporary step-down payment when a modest pay increase would abruptly end a qualifying subsidy.
measure: Change in take-home resources after the raise and program cost.
question: How would the state identify the point where a raise leaves a household with less and decide when the extra payment ends?

title: Offer a lawyer before eviction court
action: Counties fund timely legal representation for eligible tenants starting when a notice arrives.
measure: Cases with representation before the first hearing and involuntary moves.
question: How could someone reach a lawyer after receiving a notice while there is still time to prepare for the hearing?

title: Let each bus fare count toward a pass
action: Transit agencies cap daily and monthly charges at the relevant pass price as riders pay trip by trip, including with a cash-reloadable card.
measure: Extra fare paid compared with buying the same pass in advance.
question: Where could a cash rider reload a card, and how would transfers count toward the daily or monthly cap?
aliases: bus pass costs too much upfront

title: Make counseling appointments affordable
action: County clinics contract for sliding-fee counseling slots that people can book directly, with some appointments outside work hours.
measure: Days to a first completed visit and what the patient paid.
question: Which appointment times would people be able to keep, and how would they learn the price before booking?

title: Match grocery benefits spent on produce
action: Local food programs and grocers match eligible fruit and vegetable purchases up to a posted amount.
measure: Match dollars used by households and cost per participating store.
question: How would shoppers know what qualifies and see the match before they decide what to buy?

title: Give family caregivers a regular break
action: Counties purchase bookable hours of respite care for people looking after an older or disabled relative.
measure: Requested care hours delivered and time on the waiting list.
question: How could a caregiver book someone qualified for their relative's needs and arrange backup if that person cancels?
aliases: need a break caring for mom
help caring for disabled family member

title: Hire for skills when a degree is optional
action: Public employers remove unnecessary degree screens and assess candidates against published job skills while retaining required licenses.
measure: Qualified hires and six-month retention.
question: For a job that needs no license, what work sample could show someone can do it without an expensive application process?

title: Fix dangerous crossings on the way to work
action: Cities select a crossing with people who use it and test safer signal timing, lighting or a refuge island based on the site.
measure: Crossing time and observed conflicts before and after.
question: Which crossing do workers find hardest to use, and how would the city check what changes during an early or late shift?
aliases: can't cross the street in time
walking to work in the dark

title: Keep utilities on in dangerous weather
action: Utilities and regulators set clear heat and cold triggers for pausing disconnections and offer a repayment path when the danger passes.
measure: Homes disconnected during a trigger and arrears afterward.
question: Who would trigger the pause, reach households already scheduled for shutoff, and set a workable repayment date?
aliases: power shut off in a heat wave

title: Bridge health coverage when a job ends
action: States pilot short-term premium help for eligible people who lose job coverage and are moving to another plan.
measure: Uninsured days between plans and cost per person helped.
question: How could the program start help before coverage lapses and stop it when the next plan begins?

title: Give outdoor workers paid heat breaks
action: Employers and public contractors test heat-triggered paid rest, drinking water and accessible shade using worksite conditions.
measure: Breaks provided and heat-related incidents per shift.
question: Who would call a heat break on site, and how would someone paid by the piece receive their break pay?

title: Cover the up-front cost of starting a trade
action: Workforce boards pay eligible exam fees and starter-tool costs before the first paycheck, while preserving employers' existing obligations.
measure: Workers who start the job and their remaining up-front cost.
question: Which costs can the board pay directly before someone starts, and which belong to the employer?

title: Put urgent rental repairs on a deadline
action: City inspectors triage conditions such as lost heat or water, assign a repair deadline and verify the work with tenants.
measure: Days to a verified repair and repeat failures.
question: How would an inspector prioritize a home without heat and confirm with the tenant that the repair held?
aliases: my landlord won't fix the heat
no hot water in my apartment
example: Imagine waking up in a rental with no heat and no date for a repair.

title: Give rural workers a shared ride to their shift
action: Regional employers and transit providers pilot shift-timed vanpools on routes without practical bus service.
measure: Completed round trips per week and cost per rider.
question: Which pickup points work for people on the same shift, and who would cover the drive home if overtime runs late?
aliases: ride from the country to work

title: Offer retirement saving through payroll
action: States offer a portable, low-fee payroll savings option to workers without a workplace plan, with clear fees and an easy opt-out.
measure: Participation after one year and fees paid by savers.
question: How could someone check the fees, change their contribution or keep the account when they change jobs?
aliases: my job has no retirement plan

title: Hear claims of retaliation for organizing sooner
action: Federal lawmakers fund expedited independent hearings for workers alleging retaliation for organizing, with time for employers to respond.
measure: Median time to a hearing and to an enforceable decision.
question: How would hearings move sooner while giving both workers and employers time to gather and challenge evidence?

title: Stop asking families for the same paperwork
action: Benefits agencies let applicants choose to reuse verified documents across permitted programs, with phone and paper alternatives.
measure: Repeat document requests and time to finish an application.
question: How would applicants choose which programs may reuse a document and correct it when circumstances change?
aliases: they keep asking for my pay stubs

title: Offer basic home internet at one clear price
action: Local governments negotiate a low-cost plan with providers that includes equipment and states the ongoing monthly price.
measure: Total paid after a year and actual service reliability.
question: Which equipment and fees would the quoted price include, and how could a household challenge a higher bill?

title: Make urgent dental care affordable
action: Counties purchase urgent appointments at community dental clinics for uninsured adults at a published sliding fee.
measure: Wait to treatment and patient cost per visit.
question: How could an uninsured patient get an urgent slot and know what treatment the quoted fee covers?

title: Make free tax filing available after work
action: Libraries and qualified tax-help partners offer evening and weekend filing appointments for eligible households.
measure: Completed returns and out-of-pocket preparation fees.
question: Which evenings would tax preparers cover, and how could someone check what documents to bring before making the trip?

title: Keep starter homes affordable at resale
action: Local land trusts retain ownership of the land and sell homes under a clear resale formula buyers can evaluate before purchase.
measure: Buyer housing cost and affordability for the next buyer.
question: How much of a future price increase would go to the first buyer, and what could the next buyer afford under that formula?

title: Let families receive a child tax credit monthly
action: A state pilots an optional monthly payment of a refundable child credit, with simple income updates and a hardship process for overpayments.
measure: Payment reliability, overpayments and household cash shortfalls.
question: How could a family update its income midyear, and what would happen if monthly payments turn out to be too high?
aliases: wait for tax refund for kids

title: Give employees a share of company profits
action: Employers pilot a published profit-sharing formula on top of agreed base wages, including hourly staff, with a clear explanation when no payout is due.
measure: Actual payouts across wage levels and base wages over time.
question: Which earnings and hours would count in the formula, and how could an hourly worker check their share?
